record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Is the free product of R∗ groups also R∗ ?

evidence.quote: 3.3∗ . (V. M. Kopytov, N. Ya. Medvedev [83] Problem 16.49) Is the free product of R∗ groups also R∗ ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called right-orderable if there exists a total order $\le$ on $G$ that is invariant under right multiplication, i.e. $a\le b$ implies $ac\le bc$ for all $a,b,c\in G$. Following Kopytov–Medvedev, denote by $\mathcal{R}^{*}$ the class of right-orderable groups $G$ admitting a right-invariant total order $\le$ such that every $\le$-convex subgroup of $G$ is normal in $G$ (a subgroup $C\le G$ is convex with respect to $\le$ if, whenever $c_1\le g\le c_2$ with $c_1,c_2\in C$, then $g\in C$). Equivalently, $G\in\mathcal{R}^{*}$ if and only if $G$ admits a right order whose system of convex subgroups is a chain of normal subgroups.

Question: If $G_1,G_2\in\mathcal{R}^{*}$, is the free product $G_1*G_2$ (in the category of groups) again a member of $\mathcal{R}^{*}$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for the closure of the Kopytov–Medvedev class $\mathcal{R}^{*}$ under free products (Kourovka Notebook problem 16.49) did not turn up a published resolution. Standard references on right-ordered groups discuss closure of right-orderability under free products (Vinogradov-type results), but no source consulted asserts a positive or negative answer for the class $\mathcal{R}^{*}$ specifically. Status appears to remain undetermined from available sources.
